note: An attacker-controlled glyph id from shaping is forwarded into the CBDT accelerator when glyf extents are unavailable.
The glyph selects a CBLC index subtable record and also yields the base pointer for the containing CBLC table.
The record is asked to resolve extents using the table base, but the vulnerable implementation ignores that base in the callee.
The fix shows the intended propagation: the subtable offset is relative to the CBLC base, not the record object.
In the vulnerable version, the same offset is applied relative to the record address, redirecting the read to attacker-influenced out-of-bounds memory.

note: The miscomputed pointer is interpreted as an IndexSubtable, so its header controls the subsequent parsing path.
If the forged subtable/image format path is accepted, bitmap metrics are read from the wrong location and copied into the output extents, producing the memory-safety sink.
